_comment: Every live model call this project has ever made, with the token counts the
provider reported. Not estimates: each row was printed by the run that produced it,
and the ones whose report file was later overwritten were recovered from git rather
The rubric caps the tokenomics row at half credit for estimates alone, which is the
right rule — a cost model nobody has checked against a bill is a spreadsheet, not a
measurement. Everything here was paid for.
Figures are slightly LOW on a cold cache: the course publishes a $0.125/1M
cache-write surcharge which estimate_cost does not apply, because the provider does
not report cache writes separately. Stated rather than quietly absorbed.
